slides.headline: MAINTENANCE AGREEMENTS: THE MATH NOBODY SHOWS YOU
slides.body: The difference between a shop that survives shoulder season and one that sweats it.

slides.headline: THE PROBLEM
slides.body: Calls drop 30–40% every shoulder season. Overhead drops 0%. 40% of owners call cash flow their #1 problem. Feast pays for famine — barely.

slides.headline: THE FIX: 200 CLUB MEMBERS
slides.body: 200 members × $180–$240/yr = $36,000–$48,000/yr of revenue that arrives whether the weather cooperates or not. Two visits each — scheduled in YOUR slow months, on purpose.

slides.headline: THE HIDDEN PAYOFF IS BIGGER
slides.body: Club members call YOU first — no Angi, no shopping around. Tune-ups surface repairs and aging systems early. Industry rule of thumb: members are worth several times a one-time customer over the life of the equipment (replacements land with the shop that's been in the house twice a year).

slides.headline: SO WHY DO MOST SHOPS HAVE ALMOST NO MEMBERS?
slides.body: Because enrollment lives in the tech's memory ("mention the club if you think of it") and renewals live in nobody's. It's a follow-through problem, not a sales problem.

slides.headline: WHAT THE AUTOMATED VERSION LOOKS LIKE
slides.body: • Post-job text offers the plan while the visit is fresh • Spring/fall enrollment campaign to your whole list • Auto-scheduled member visits in slow weeks • Renewal reminders that never forget. Runs on the customer list you already own.

slides.headline: 200 MEMBERS DOESN'T HAPPEN BY ACCIDENT
slides.body: It happens 5–10 enrollments a week, automatically. Tomorrow I'm posting a screen recording: AI writing your entire fall tune-up campaign in 90 seconds. Follow so you don't miss it — or comment CLUB and I'll send you the enrollment-sequence outline.
